lines.text: Fibonacci isn't a formula to memorise. It's an instruction you can follow with a pencil.
Every number is the two before it, added together. That's it.
So let's just do it. Start with zero and one.
Zero, one. Add them — that's one.
Now the last two, one and one — two.
Last two again, one and two — three.
Zero, one, one, two, three, five, eight, thirteen. You've just done Fibonacci, and you never needed a formula.
Now notice what your hand was actually doing, because this is the part the code has to copy.
You weren't holding the whole list in your head. You only ever had two numbers at a time — the last one, and the one before it.
That middle line is the one that looks hard, so let's take it slowly. It's a shuffle.
The one that was second becomes first. And the sum becomes the new second.
Both at the same instant — and that bit matters. If you moved one of them first, you'd have written over the number you still needed to do the adding with.
So the pair goes: zero and one. Then one and one. Then one and two. Then two and three.
Say that out loud, and it's the same pencil you were using a minute ago.
